issues.body: `_normalize_path_entry` still does not canonicalize internal `.` or `..` segments. GitHub Actions resolves `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` to the workspace-root divergence log, but `_glob_to_re` compares the unnormalized spelling to the root-relative target and returns false. The new `coverage-${{ matrix.shard }}/../...` fixture is not a regression test for this case: it is classified as unresolved dynamic input and returns true conservatively before dot-segment matching is exercised.
issues.fix_hint: Lexically normalize static workspace-relative entries against a synthetic workspace root before glob matching, resolving `.` and `..` without destroying glob metacharacters; treat paths escaping the workspace conservatively. Add positive fixtures for `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` and `foo/./../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json`, plus a directory form normalizing to the workspace root and an escaping-path case.
issues.title: Static dot-segment upload paths still bypass artifact detection

verdict.summary: Round 4 leaves the prior major finding unresolved. `_normalize_path_entry` still removes only leading `./` and trailing `/`; it does not lexically resolve internal `.` or `..` segments. The added traversal-shaped fixture is dynamic (`${{ matrix.shard }}`), so it passes only because unresolved expressions are conservatively treated as includes and does not test the static bypass. A statically resolvable upload path such as `target/../coverage-cone-divergence-shard-1.json` still names the workspace-root log at runtime while the matcher reports that it does not. Progress is stagnant because the same major defect remains at the same severity.
